- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 1–3% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 1–2% for 10–15 day horizons.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.5), model lags in reversal — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce slope.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture mean reversion — add 1–2% downward bias to later days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., -0.3 to -0.5) and price is flat, model tends to forecast downward drift — avoid negative bias unless confirmed by technical indicators.
